topics.topic: Exact multipart length arithmetic and handling of malformed or inconsistent framing
questions: When may this subtraction be trusted, and what is returned when the body has an epilogue, another part, a missing or non-final delimiter, a different permitted line ending, a mismatched declared request length, or a result that is negative?
Exactly which bytes belong to the head and closing delimiter for this subtraction, especially the CRLF immediately before the boundary and the optional final line ending?

What must upload_framing do when a declared request length is smaller than the known head plus closing delimiter, disagrees with the body actually received, or includes bytes after the closing delimiter?

quotes:
and the file part's declared length — the request's declared length less
the head it read and the closing delimiter with its final `--` and line end,
or none when the request declares none — so that a file of exactly the
import limit is not refused for its framing (A19 rule 4).
judgement.why: Exact multipart byte arithmetic, delimiter syntax, epilogues, additional parts and malformed framing are encoding and contract questions belonging to State 6, not State 3 module ownership.

topics.topic: Module ownership of session-cookie construction, attributes, serialization, creation, and invalidation
questions: Which module owns each cookie decision: creation and invalidation, attributes such as Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite/path, origin scoping, and serialization into HTTP responses?
Which module owns the cookie attributes and construction required by A13 rule 1: owner_sessions or owner_interface?

quotes:
`module:owner_sessions`. Sign the owner in with the owner credential under
the instance's lockout, making a new owner session (A13 rules 1, 3, 4).

The new session's identity and its CSRF value, or `unauthenticated`
(`sign_in_refused`).

On sign-in, the session cookie set: not readable by scripts, only to
Registry's origin, and always HTTPS-only (A13 rule 1; owner, 2026-11-17). Registry never expires or deletes the cookie: an ended session's
cookie is refused at the session check and replaced by the next sign-in, so
no answer, however late it arrives, can remove a newer session's cookie.
judgement.why: The later operation texts assign session creation and identity to owner_sessions while owner_interface sets and serializes the cookie and deliberately performs no cookie invalidation.

topics.topic: Ownership and timing of request arrival, multipart-head reading, and session admission
questions: Which module owns the definition and sequencing of request arrival, multipart-head reading, and the call to the session check, given that `owner_sessions` does not list `operations` or `upload_framing` under Knows and may not know later module `operations`?
Is arrival the network/request arrival before body-head reading, or the later handoff to owner_sessions after upload_framing has read the multipart head?

quotes:
the arrival of an
owner request, which is the moment `operations` hands it to the session
check — after its headers and, for an upload, the head `upload_framing`
read, at most `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES` — where `owner_sessions` takes the
monotonic reading its validity is checked at (rule 2);

An owner
   request is any request to the owner interface that
   carries the valid session, whatever its answer; its arrival restarts the 30
   minutes — of concurrent requests the latest arrival counts; before the
   first request it runs from the sign-in. Validity is
   checked when a request arrives (A04 rule 6, stage 1); a request that
   passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs, and
   a restart that interrupts it leaves nothing of it (A04 rule 4).
judgement.divergence: A slow upload beginning while the session is valid is either admitted at network/request arrival and completes, or is checked only after its multipart head is read and is refused if the session expires meanwhile; the owner observes mapping versus sign-in refusal.
judgement.why: State 3 moves arrival and the validity reading until after multipart-head reading, while State 2 says validity is checked when the request arrives and an admitted request completes after a later limit.

judgement.why: State 2 requires the declared upload length to be checked before any byte is read, but State 3 makes the relevant declared length derivable only after upload_framing has read the multipart head.

quotes:
Any check of the CSRF value (`owner_sessions`), the size limit of the file
and its reading (`migration_import`, A19 rule 4), the HTTP server and its
